summary: Admit one bounded, approval-bound PЭК return-to-sender operation for an accepted cargo.

impacts.evidence: The existing return-logistics operation and account lookup remain organization/workspace scoped before provider egress.
Basic credentials and the provider description stay outside Core, operation receipts and audit records.
The existing return-logistics API is reused without a breaking schema change; only the admitted provider capability expands.
The existing commerce.returns.logistics_requested.v1 worker event carries the new admitted adapter path.
The existing LogisticsReturnCreator interface is implemented by the PEK connector and resolved only by the built-in registry.
The existing return-logistics repository and operation receipt store the normalized result.
Capability, active account, approval, callback-scoped SecretProvider and one numeric cargo code are independent gates.
The existing return-logistics create route and worker require the enabled write-sensitive return capability and approval policy.
The existing returns mutation and worker audit lineage records the operation without provider payload.
Existing durable operation state distinguishes success, confirmed rejection and unknown provider outcome; no automatic duplicate side effect is introduced.
The host calls only the documented fixed ПЭК endpoint and does not accept a caller-controlled provider URL.
The existing worker error classification exposes bounded retryable, permanent and unknown outcomes.
Capability removal closes admission; a provider return is not silently reversed by the host.
Deterministic adapter, host transport, runtime admission and existing worker tests cover success, rejection and scope boundaries.

follow_up_tasks: Live qualification with a disposable accepted cargo and queued-result reconciliation
